slides.heading: Relation
slides.body: A relation pairs elements of set A with elements of set B. Not every relation is a function.

slides.heading: Function rule
slides.body: Each input has exactly one output. Vertical line test on graphs.

slides.heading: Domain and range
slides.body: Domain: allowed inputs. Range: actual outputs produced.

slides.heading: Worked idea
slides.body: f(x)=x²+1. Domain: all real x. f(2)=5.

slides.heading: Try this
slides.body: Is x ↦ ±√x a function of x≥0? No — two outputs for one input (except 0).

slides.heading: Degree
slides.body: Highest power with nonzero coefficient. Degree 2 → quadratic.

slides.heading: End behaviour
slides.body: Even degree, positive leading coefficient → both ends up.

slides.heading: Factor theorem
slides.body: If f(a)=0 then (x−a) is a factor.

slides.heading: Worked idea
slides.body: f(x)=x²−5x+6=(x−2)(x−3). Roots 2 and 3.

slides.heading: Try this
slides.body: Degree of 4x³ − x + 7 is 3.

slides.heading: Exponential growth
slides.body: y = a·bˣ with b>1 grows; 0<b<1 decays.

slides.heading: Log definition
slides.body: log_b a = c ⇔ b^c = a (a>0, b>0, b≠1).

slides.heading: Log laws
slides.body: log(xy)=log x + log y; log(x/y)=log x − log y; log(xⁿ)=n log x.

slides.heading: Worked idea
slides.body: log₂ 32 = 5 because 2⁵=32.

slides.heading: Try this
slides.body: Simplify log 100 + log 1 (common log). log 100=2; log 1=0 → 2.

slides.heading: Newton’s first law
slides.body: An object stays at rest or in uniform motion unless a net force acts.

slides.heading: Newton’s second law
slides.body: F = ma. Unit of force: newton (N).

slides.heading: Newton’s third law
slides.body: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.

slides.heading: Worked idea
slides.body: m=2 kg, a=3 m/s² → F=6 N.

slides.heading: Try this
slides.body: If net force is zero, acceleration is zero.

slides.heading: Work
slides.body: W = F·d (force along displacement). Unit: joule (J).

slides.heading: Kinetic energy
slides.body: KE = ½mv².

slides.heading: Potential energy
slides.body: GPE = mgh near Earth.

slides.heading: Worked idea
slides.body: m=2 kg, v=3 m/s → KE = 9 J.

slides.heading: Try this
slides.body: Raise 1 kg by 2 m (g≈10): GPE≈20 J.

slides.heading: Wave equation
slides.body: v = fλ (speed = frequency × wavelength).

slides.heading: Transverse vs longitudinal
slides.body: Transverse: perpendicular vibration. Longitudinal: parallel (sound in air).

slides.heading: Sound
slides.body: Needs a medium; cannot travel in vacuum.

slides.heading: Try this
slides.body: Higher pitch means higher frequency.

slides.heading: Unit circle idea
slides.body: sin and cos relate coordinates on a circle of radius 1.

slides.heading: Right-triangle ratios
slides.body: SOH-CAH-TOA still applies.

slides.heading: Pythagorean identity
slides.body: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.

slides.heading: Worked idea
slides.body: If sinθ=3/5, cosθ=4/5 in a 3-4-5 triangle.

slides.heading: Try this
slides.body: tanθ = sinθ/cosθ.

slides.heading: Mean
slides.body: Sum of values ÷ number of values.

slides.heading: Median
slides.body: Middle value when ordered.

slides.heading: Mode
slides.body: Most frequent value.

slides.heading: Worked idea
slides.body: Data 2,3,3,7: mean=3.75, median=3, mode=3.

slides.heading: Try this
slides.body: Which is resistant to outliers? Median.

slides.heading: Mitosis
slides.body: Produces two identical diploid cells for growth and repair.

slides.heading: Meiosis
slides.body: Produces gametes with half the chromosome number.

slides.heading: Stages of mitosis
slides.body: Prophase → metaphase → anaphase → telophase.

slides.heading: Worked idea
slides.body: Human body cells have 46 chromosomes; gametes have 23.

slides.heading: Try this
slides.body: Crossing over occurs in meiosis, not mitosis.

slides.heading: Gene and allele
slides.body: Gene: unit of heredity. Alleles: alternative forms of a gene.

slides.heading: Dominant vs recessive
slides.body: Dominant shows in heterozygote; recessive needs two copies.

slides.heading: Punnett square
slides.body: Tool to predict offspring genotype ratios.

slides.heading: Worked idea
slides.body: Tt × Tt → 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt (phenotypic 3:1 if T dominant).

slides.heading: Try this
slides.body: Homozygous means two identical alleles.
